original_value: Mass cytometry (CyTOF) has become a method of choice for in-depth characterization of tissue heterogeneity in health and disease, and is currently implemented in multiple clinical trials, where higher quality standards must be met. Currently, preprocessing of raw files is commonly performed in independent standalone tools, which makes it difficult to reproduce. Here, we present an R pipeline based on an updated version of CATALYST that covers all preprocessing steps required for downstream mass cytometry analysis in a fully reproducible way. This new version of CATALYST is based on Bioconductor’s SingleCellExperiment class and fully unit tested. The R-based pipeline includes file concatenation, bead-based normalization, single-cell deconvolution, spillover compensation and live cell gating after debris and doublet removal. Importantly, this pipeline also includes different quality checks to assess machine sensitivity and staining performance while allowing also for batch correction. This pipeline is based on open source R packages and can be easily be adapted to different study designs. It therefore has the potential to significantly facilitate the work of CyTOF users while increasing the quality and reproducibility of data generated with this technology.

result.paraphrase: Mass cytometry (CyTOF) has emerged as a preferred approach for detailed profiling of tissue heterogeneity in both health and disease, and is now used in multiple clinical trials that require higher quality standards. At present, raw-file preprocessing is typically done with separate standalone tools, which hinders reproducibility. We present an R pipeline built on an updated CATALYST version that performs all preprocessing steps needed for downstream mass cytometry analysis in a fully reproducible manner. This new CATALYST release is built on Bioconductor’s SingleCellExperiment class and is fully unit tested. The R-based workflow covers file concatenation, bead-based normalization, single-cell deconvolution, spillover compensation, and live-cell gating after debris and doublet removal. Importantly, it also provides quality checks to evaluate machine sensitivity and staining performance, while enabling batch correction. Based on open-source R packages, the pipeline can be readily adapted to different study designs. It therefore has the potential to greatly streamline work for CyTOF users while improving the quality and reproducibility of data produced with this technology.
